note: The trader's own tokens, laid over the core's (dayz-mcp.toml, [build] tokens: the core's file first, this one second). The core gives the type of the series and its palette; the trade screen wears a palette of its own (the owner, 2026-11-11: colours as in the trade screen of STALKER 2; colours only, nothing of that game's art): near-black panels, thin grey frames, white text, orange for what matters, green for what the player gets, dark red for what the trader does not take. The colours that also name the series' palette (panel, edge, accent and the rest) are overridden here for the trader's layouts alone. Beside them, what a trade screen has and the PDA does not: the bed of an item grid, the tile on it, the strip a panel's title stands on, the colour of a price, the veil under a dialog, the seam around a slot, and two larger sizes for sums.
